about: Hand-labelled cases for the skill-matching rule (W-1). Each case fixes the requirements of a posting and the evidence of a resume, and states which requirements a careful human reader would call met. Extraction is deliberately not measured here: the lists are given, so the only thing under test is how a requirement is compared with what a resume evidences. The cases cover several trades on purpose -- the application is for a cook and a mechanic as much as for a backend engineer, and a rule tuned on one vocabulary fails quietly on the others.
labelled_by: Claude, 2026-09-02 -- review before trusting any number computed from this

cases.resume: Backend engineer. Built REST APIs in Python with FastAPI. Modelled and tuned schemas in PostgreSQL and wrote the reporting queries by hand.
cases.notes: Nobody tunes PostgreSQL schemas and writes reporting queries without SQL. The word itself never appears in the resume, which is the whole point of the case.

cases.resume: Analyst. Wrote complex SQL reports against a MySQL warehouse.
cases.notes: The asymmetry that makes this hard: PostgreSQL implies SQL, SQL implies no particular database. A rule that reads implication in both directions is worse than the one we have.

cases.resume: Ran PostgreSQL in production for four years, including replication and backups.
cases.notes: A trap for similarity by embedding: these two terms sit close together in vector space and are not the same skill.

cases.resume: Frontend developer working in JavaScript and TypeScript with React.
cases.notes: Guards over-matching. A substring rule fails here, and so does a model asked to be helpful.

cases.resume: Ran services on k8s in production and wrote the Dockerfiles for them.
cases.notes: The abbreviation was already expanded when the resume was stored, so this case should pass today. It is here to catch a change that breaks what works.

cases.resume: Ran services on k8s in production and wrote the Dockerfiles for them.
cases.notes: The same resume with no LLM reading of it -- the configuration CI and a keyless machine run in. k8s is kubernetes to any human reader.

cases.resume: Wrote unit and integration tests for every service; the suite runs on each push.
cases.notes: The case W-1 recorded on real data. Python is genuinely absent and must stay missing.

cases.resume: Set up GitHub Actions to build, test and deploy the service on every merge to main.
cases.notes: A pipeline that builds, tests and deploys on merge is CI/CD, whatever the posting calls it.

cases.resume: Deployed services to AWS (ECS, RDS) and managed the infrastructure with Terraform.
cases.notes: AWS is a cloud platform. ECS is not Kubernetes, which is the half of this case that keeps the label honest.

cases.resume: Packaged every service as a Docker image and shipped it to a private registry.
cases.notes: The example the extraction prompt itself uses, seen from the matching side.

cases.resume: Backend services in Go, plus a command-line tool in Rust.
cases.notes: Two names for one language. Python is absent and stays absent.

cases.resume: Ten years of Python 3, mostly Django and Celery.
cases.notes: The limit the code documents in cover(): python and python3 are different terms to a deterministic rule and the same skill to a reader.

cases.resume: Maintained the message queue consumers and the RabbitMQ cluster behind them.
cases.notes: A multi-word requirement the current rule already handles. Kafka is a different broker and is missing.

cases.resume: Led a team of four and mentored two juniors through their first year.
cases.notes: Public speaking is nowhere in this resume. A model looking for something to award tends to find it here.

cases.resume: Data scientist. Trained forecasting models in R and presented the results to the finance team.
cases.notes: The floor. A score of 0.0 has to stay reachable: a matcher that awards partial credit to everyone stops ranking anything.

cases.resume: Office administrator. Kept the department budget in Excel, built the monthly reports and the pivot tables the board reads.
cases.notes: Excel is a spreadsheet. The same shape as postgresql answering sql, in an office rather than a server room.

cases.resume: Warehouse operative. Operated a forklift on every shift for three years and ran the quarterly stock counts.
cases.notes: Arguable and worth arguing about: nobody drives a forklift on shift for three years without the licence, but this label reads a credential out of experience. If you disagree, this is the case to change.

cases.resume: Line cook in a hotel kitchen. Ran the cold starters section, kept the HACCP records and the fridge temperature logs.
cases.notes: HACCP is a food safety system; keeping its records is the evidence. Sous vide is a technique this kitchen never mentions.

cases.resume: Car mechanic, six years in an independent garage. Replaced brakes and clutches, read fault codes with the diagnostic computer, seasonal tyre changes.
cases.notes: The multi-word rule needs every word present: the resume has diagnostics but not vehicle, brakes but not systems. Trade postings name the same work with a different noun on the end.

cases.resume: Shop assistant. Served customers at the till, took cash and card payments and did the daily cash-up.
cases.notes: A till is a point-of-sale system; the posting uses the retail-chain word and the resume the shop-floor one. Nothing in this resume touches replenishment.

cases.resume: Care assistant in a residential home. Helped residents with washing, dressing and meals, and kept the daily care notes.
cases.notes: The trap in this trade: helping with meals is not giving medication, which is a regulated task with its own training. A model looking for something to award will award it.

cases.resume: Delivery driver, three years of city courier work on a category B licence.
cases.notes: Credentials are pass or fail and one-directional, like sql and postgresql: C+E implies B, B implies nothing about C+E.

cases.resume: Ran the onboarding workshops for every new hire and wrote the materials they were taught from.
cases.notes: Deliberately in tension with mentoring-and-leadership, where public speaking is not met: running workshops is speaking to a room, mentoring two juniors is not. Curriculum design is left unmet -- writing materials is close to it and not the same job.

cases.resume: Accounts assistant. Booked purchase invoices in SAP, reconciled the bank statements and prepared the VAT return.
cases.notes: SAP is an ERP. Payroll is a different desk in the same office and this resume never sat at it.

cases.resume: Security guard with a valid first aid certificate and a clean driving licence.
cases.notes: One word, two spellings, two continents. Non-IT postings are full of them -- licence/license, tyre/tire, organise/organize -- and a token comparison sees two different words.

cases.resume: Waiter in a seaside hotel through four seasons; served German and British guests in their own languages.
cases.notes: Should pass today: the extracted list carries both languages. Here so the non-IT half of the dataset is not only failures.
